payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Stuffing the paper into the cup
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Can the edited scene be visually inventoried to locate the paper and candidate receiving object and describe their visible boundaries and occlusions for a narrower insertion investigation?
node.criteria: Pass if visible evidence permits a grounded inventory of the paper and candidate receiving object, including concrete boundaries, visible identifying features, overlap, and visibility limitations. A pass establishes inspectable context only, not confirmed cup identity or insertion. Report separately whether paper identity and cup identity are established, disproved, or unresolved. Fail if adequate visibility positively establishes absence of the paper or any relevant receiving object; identify the decisive evidence. Unknown if framing or visibility prevents even a grounded inventory. Unresolved cup identity must be recorded explicitly and never silently promoted to confirmed identity.
node.binding: Inspect source and edit directly. Use the source only to locate the requested objects and compare appearances, not to certify the reddish object's identity. Describe the paper outline and the reddish object's exposed contour and dark marking; investigate whether these support a cup, another object, or neither determination. Consider the combined visible structure without demanding a visible interior as an absolute identity requirement. Distinguish image-plane overlap from entry into a container. Do not infer hidden geometry or stuffing from the hand's grip.

node_traces.evidence: The edited scene is clear enough to inventory. The paper is a blue-and-white printed sheet with a roughly rectangular outline, held by a hand; its lower and side edges are visible, while the hand covers part of its upper-left area. A reddish rounded object is partly exposed behind the paper on the right, with a curved outer contour and a dark line across it. The paper overlaps the object in the image plane, but the visible evidence does not establish that the object is a cup or that the paper enters it. Paper identity: established. Cup identity: unresolved; the exposed contour and marking are insufficient to distinguish a cup from another object.

The reddish object has an exposed curved contour and a dark line across it, but no clearly visible rim or opening; its identity as a cup is unresolved. The paper is identifiable as the requested paper, while the candidate receiving object's cup identity is unresolved. The overlap is image-plane overlap only; entry into a container is not established.
